chapter_note: The chapter opens with a hagiographic speech frame and closes with institutional/eschatological application (notably pastoral drift in ¶4–5). The oldest layer is concentrated in ¶2–3: impersonal cosmological description of the Mother of Life and the First Man grieving for their children/sons amid the Darkness, ruling-power, and enemy assault. ¶4 shifts to Mani’s church-mission register (holy church, persecution, Light Mind) and ¶5 to Christian eschatological vocabulary (gehenna, repentance).

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogue attribution (“Once again the enlightener speaks to his disciples”) marks the redactional container; the first-person self-identification functions as part of the hagiographic setup rather than impersonal cosmological exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.147⟩ The first who grieves is the first Mother of Life. She is sad because of her children who are set in affliction, for they were conjoined with the Darkness and the [poi]son. They have been bound with the entire ruling-power. For what was she grieving, [wa]tching over them taking these afflictions? Whenever she might [s]ee them and how suffering is brought upon them, she shall grieve and be unhappy on account of them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal, system-internal cosmological description (Mother of Life; her children; Darkness; ruling-power) with no institutional address or citation; grief is explained as a function of cosmic bondage/affliction.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.148⟩ [The s]econd one who is troubled of heart is the First Man, whose [great]ness and kingdom is established in the li[ght] ship [...]. And he too is troubled of heart because of his five sons who are set in the midst of danger. For any time he may see that they are given trouble, always he might hear the sound of their weeping as they cry out because of the blows and wounds of the enemy who assaults them daily; and as he sees them like this constantly, he shall g[ri]eve and mourn on account of his [s]o[n]s.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Classic core register: named cosmological figure (First Man) situated in a cosmic locale (“light ship”) and a systematic grouping (“five sons”), describing ongoing Light–Darkness conflict mechanics without exhortation or church-reference.

Shifts from cosmic system to Mani’s institutional present: “holy church,” mission claim (“I chose”), persecution, and the implantation of “Light Mind” in the church—cosmos→community identification typical of editorial/institutional application.

Uses Christian eschatological and penitential vocabulary (“gehenna,” “repentance,” ‘for ever’) and a salvific offer attributed to the speaker; this material most plausibly enters via Manichaean Christian synthesis rather than the pre-compilation cosmological substrate.
